dimension_marks.reason: Connects competition for colonies and nationalism to European rivalry.
Explains armed preparedness and how alliances widened a local conflict.
Names Franz Ferdinand, Sarajevo and June 1914, but omits 28 June.
Correctly states Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, but omits the ultimatum and 28 July.
Correctly links Germany's invasion of Belgium to British entry, but does not describe Russian mobilization and German declarations.
Correctly identifies Britain, France and Russia as the main Entente powers.
Places Germany and Austria-Hungary together in the opposing camp.
Distinguishes Italy's pre-war alliance, neutrality in 1914 and Allied entry in 1915.
Correctly dates Ottoman entry to 1914 and places Bulgaria on the same side, but omits Bulgaria's 1915 entry year.
Correctly gives US entry alongside the Allies in 1917.
Places protective trenches on the Western Front after the early fighting in 1914.
Connects both machine guns and artillery to danger for exposed attackers.
Explains that barbed wire slowed soldiers in no man's land and increased their vulnerability.
Links high casualties and very small gains to the stuck front.
Mentions protection alongside mud, rats and disease.
Gives 1917 but omits the declaration date of 6 April.
Connects renewed unrestricted submarine attacks to US entry in 1917.
Explains the telegram's proposed German alliance with Mexico against the US.
Identifies money, supplies and troops, and explicitly recognizes other Allied contributions.
Distinguishes the 11 November 1918 ceasefire from later peace, including Versailles in 1919.
Gives 28 June 1919 and Germany, but does not identify the Allied and Associated signatories.
Identifies European territorial loss through Alsace-Lorraine and loss of overseas colonies.
Accurately gives the 100,000 army limit and air-force prohibition.
Connects reparations to Article 231's responsibility clause.
Explains German resentment and rejects inevitable-war reasoning, but omits the League of Nations.
Explains nationalism and imperial competition as causes of rivalry and mistrust.
Explains militarism and how alliances widened a regional crisis.
Correctly identifies Franz Ferdinand's assassination at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914.
Connects Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia with its 28 July declaration.
Explains Russian mobilization, German declarations against Russia and France, and Belgium's invasion followed by British entry.
Correctly places Britain, France and Russia in the 1914 Entente.
Identifies Germany and Austria-Hungary as the Central Powers' core.
Distinguishes the pre-war alliance, neutrality in 1914 and Italy's 1915 Allied entry.
Correctly places Ottoman entry in late 1914 and Bulgarian entry in 1915 on the Central side.
Correctly identifies US entry in 1917 alongside the Allies as an associated power.
Describes opposing Western Front trench systems developing after the mobile campaigns of 1914.
Explains the defensive advantage of machine guns and artillery against exposed advancing troops.
Connects exposed no man's land and barbed-wire delay to vulnerable attackers.
Explains costly offensives, small gains and difficulty sustaining an advance through further defenses.
Explains shelter from fire alongside mud, rats, disease and sanitation problems.
Correctly gives the declaration against Germany on 6 April 1917.
Explains renewed unrestricted submarine warfare's threat to shipping and American interests.
Accurately explains the telegram's proposed German-Mexican alliance if America entered.
Identifies finance, supplies and troops while recognizing other Allied forces and Central difficulties.
Separates the 11 November 1918 halt in fighting from the later Versailles peace treaty.
Correctly identifies Germany and the Allied and Associated Powers signing on 28 June 1919.
Identifies Alsace-Lorraine and other territorial losses together with overseas colonies.
Accurately specifies the 100,000 army limit, prohibited conscription and air force, and Rhineland demilitarization.
Connects Article 231 responsibility to reparations and correctly notes the total came later.
Mentions the League Covenant and resentment while explaining that later crises and choices also mattered.
Correctly links nationalism and competition for colonies to European tension.
Does not explain militarism or rival alliances and discounts the role of armies.
Recognizes assassination of an Austrian prince as the trigger, but omits Franz Ferdinand's name, Sarajevo and date.
Connects the killing to Austria's war with Serbia, but omits the ultimatum and declaration date.
Recognizes German and Russian support for opposite sides as escalation, but omits France and gives a wrong reason for British entry.
Correctly groups Britain, France and Russia together.
Correctly groups Germany and Austria together in the opposing camp.
Incorrectly says Italy fought for Germany throughout the war.
Incorrectly claims Ottoman neutrality and Bulgarian alignment with France.
Correctly places America with Britain but incorrectly dates its entry to 1914.
Recognizes trenches as shelters for soldiers, but wrongly locates the Western Front in Russia and omits the period.
Explains danger from machine guns but does not mention artillery.
Does not explain barbed wire or exposed no man's land.
Substitutes unsupported ammunition shortages and an inability to attack in winter for the stalemate explanation.
Mentions hiding for protection along with mud and illness.
Does not give the year or date of US entry; 1918 describes the end of fighting instead.
Vaguely mentions attacked ships but misidentifies Pearl Harbor and never identifies German submarine warfare.
Omits the Zimmermann Telegram and proposed alliance with Mexico.
Identifies soldiers and supplies, but the explanation credits America alone with defeating Germany.
Incorrectly equates the armistice with the final Versailles peace treaty.
Dates the treaty around 1918 and does not identify the Allied signatories.
The claim that all German land went to France is materially false and colonial losses are absent.
Incorrectly claims a complete ban on German soldiers instead of restrictions on a permitted army.
Mentions payment and accepting blame, but does not explain the responsibility clause as the basis for reparations.
Only asserts an automatic, unavoidable Second World War; does not explain resentment or the League's role.
Links nationalism and colonial competition to European rivalry.
Connects growing armies to rivalry and explains how aligned groups spread the conflict.
Correctly names Franz Ferdinand's assassination, but omits Sarajevo and the date.
Correctly identifies Austria-Hungary fighting Serbia, but omits the ultimatum and 28 July.
Links Russian support for Serbia and German support for Austria-Hungary to escalation, but omits declarations, Belgium and British entry.
Correctly identifies Britain, France and Russia as the main Allied countries.
Correctly identifies Germany and Austria-Hungary as the main Central Powers.
Recognizes initial Italian neutrality and later Allied entry, but omits 1915.
Correctly puts the Ottoman Empire on Germany's side, but omits its entry year and Bulgaria's participation.
Correctly gives US entry alongside the Allies in 1917.
Describes opposing protective trenches on the Western Front, but omits their establishment in 1914.
Explains machine-gun danger but omits artillery.
Explains the exposed crossing between lines, but omits barbed wire.
Connects many casualties with little territorial gain to stalemate.
Mentions protection from trenches and muddy, difficult living conditions.
Correctly gives 1917, but omits 6 April.
Connects German submarine attacks and American interests to entry, but omits the renewed unrestricted policy.
Does not identify the Zimmermann Telegram or the proposed German-Mexican alliance.
Identifies troops and supplies as help for the Allies without claiming the US won alone.
Correctly separates the 11 November 1918 halt in fighting from subsequent peace negotiations.
Correctly connects Germany's defeat to the 1919 treaty, but omits the exact date and Allied signatories.
Mentions loss of territory but omits overseas colonies.
States that the army was reduced, but gives no concrete restriction.
Identifies reparations, but does not explain the responsibility clause.
Explains resentment and rejects a single inevitable cause of later war, but omits the League of Nations.
Does not identify nationalist tensions or imperial competition as WWI causes.
Omits militarism and rival alliances; the United Nations claim is anachronistic.
Misidentifies Franz Ferdinand as a German leader and substitutes the 1939 invasion of Poland for the assassination.
Does not describe Austria-Hungary's confrontation with Serbia.
Substitutes events from another war for the Russian-German-Belgian-British escalation.
Splits Britain and France into incorrect opposing teams and falsely says Russia did not exist.
Puts Germany with Britain and America, and omits Austria-Hungary.
Gives a false account of Italian switching after an American surrender rather than 1914 neutrality and 1915 Allied entry.
Does not identify Ottoman or Bulgarian participation.
Places America with Germany and falsely claims it surrendered in 1917.
Misdefines trenches as railway stations and the Western Front as a Pacific naval battle.
Does not describe the defensive roles of machine guns or artillery.
Omits barbed wire and exposed no man's land.
Denies stalemate and incorrectly claims airplanes quickly captured trenches.
The summer-sun explanation does not describe protection from fire or relevant trench hardships.
Incorrectly dates WWI entry to 1941.
Substitutes Pearl Harbor for German unrestricted submarine warfare.
Misidentifies Zimmermann as an American general rather than explaining the telegram.
The claim about atomic bombs on Germany gives no correct WWI contribution.
Incorrectly dates the armistice to 1945 and claims it created NATO.
Incorrectly gives 1945 and Germany-Japan as the treaty's parties.
Incorrectly says Germany gained French colonies rather than losing territory and colonies.
Claims a larger German army rather than restrictions.
Reverses reparations by saying Britain paid Germany.
Anachronistic claims about NATO and the EU and universal acceptance give no correct significance.
